title: Auth & Routing chaos benchmarks — lab notes (2026-06-16)
body:
Purpose
- Capture quick lab notes from a focused chaos/benchmarks session targeting routing + auth interactions across control plane fallbacks. Narrow scope: golden path requests + injected auth delays + route-fallbacks to cheaper model variants. Goal: find brittle coupling points and get numbers for an ops playbook.

Setup overview
- Cluster: staging-cplane-3 (us-west2) - 4x A100s (dedicated test pool)
- Runtime branch: bench/auth-routing-2026-06 (serving-runtime PR 1284)
- Traffic generator: locust script (scripts/bench/routing_auth_chaos.py) with 1000 users, 10 req/s baseline
- Auth shim: local auth-mock v0.3 (inject header latency and 5xx probability)
- Routing config: policy set to prefer low-latency region, fallback chain: model-v1 -> model-v1-quant -> model-v2-small
- Observability: console trace export + jaeger sampling at 20%; token cost meter enabled on test keys

What we toggled (experiments)
1) Baseline (no injection)
   - 10k requests over 10 minutes
   - p50: 82ms, p95: 180ms, p99: 420ms
   - Token cost: baseline unit 1.0

2) Auth header delay = 50ms fixed (simulate remote auth service)
   - p50: 135ms, p95: 320ms, p99: 790ms
   - Observed: request queues on worker threads for kernels increased, small spike in GPU memory consumption due to longer-lived KV cache lifetimes per request
   - Notes: meaningful latency inflation, routing decisions still within SLA but headroom reduced

3) Auth 50ms + 5% auth 401 (fast fail)
   - High error churn: 401s handled on control plane, retried by client (locust) once -> extra load on routing path for retries
   - p50: 150ms, p95: 410ms, higher error budget burn in test harness
   - Action: ensure retries are client-aware of auth 401 vs 5xx; control plane should not re-route 401s as capacity errors

4) Auth 200ms variable (50-300ms) + route failover to model-v1-quant after 1200ms server-side timeout
   - Observed fallbacks: 18% of requests fell back to quantized variant under tail auth spikes
   - p99 latency dropped for fallbacked requests but quality delta noted in logs (higher hallucination rate on a small prompt subset)
   - Cost: token cost delta - ~14% lower for fallbacked requests, but tail latency improved only for clients tolerating different responses

5) Simulated control plane throttling on route decision (200ms added) + auth jitter
   - End-to-end p95 collapsed to ~900ms; we observed cascading backpressure in allocator queue; some worker nodes showed small OOM churn due to amplification of queued KV cache states

Quick hypotheses and takeaways
- Auth latency amplifies per-request resource residency (KV caches and session objects stay longer) which increases tail latency beyond the added auth time. Not linear.
- Retries on 401s are often the wrong behavior; we need explicit client guidance and SDK defaults to avoid automated retries on auth failures.
- Routing fallbacks to quantized variants help cost and tail latency but may produce regressions in output quality for specific prompts. Should gate fallback by route-level quality signal + token budget delta.
- Control plane throttling (slow decision) is particularly dangerous: it causes head-of-line blocking and magnifies memory pressure on workers. Short-term mitigation: add decision timeouts with early path to a default-safe model variant.

Immediate action items (owners)
- Arjun: add a client SDK change to not auto-retry on 401 by default; include opt-in aggressive retry flag. Target: PR by 2026-06-23.
- Sofia: add a route-level quality flag to the routing catalog so fallbacks to quantized models are only allowed when quality_delta < threshold. Work with Evals team for a simple quality comparator. Target: design doc 2026-06-22.
- Chen: instrument KV cache residency metric (time-per-key) and add to console charts; helpful to correlate auth latency -> KV residency -> tail latency. Target: probe in staging by 2026-06-30.
- Maya: draft ops playbook section for "auth-induced latency" with recommended short-term mitigations and sample locust tests. Target: first draft 2026-06-20.

Open questions / discussion notes
- What is an acceptable quality delta for fallback models? (Sofia to propose a baseline threshold and quick eval harness).
- Should control plane prefer returning a 503 vs delaying routing decisions? Tradeoff: 503 exposes downstream retry behavior but avoids worker memory amplification.
- Can we batch auth checks for high-volume customers? Risk: cache staleness vs throughput gains.

Small gotchas observed (notes to self)
- Locust client retries were hiding some true 5xx counts; turn off client-side retry when measuring error rates.
- Jaeger traces for fallback paths currently lack model-version meta in spans; add tags so we can filter fallback traces easily.
- Some quantized binaries in staging were built with older kernel optimizations; mismatch caused slight perf noise in one run. Rebuild and pin kernels for next run.

Logs/snippets
- Example trace id: trace-20260616-1a2b (auth latency 243ms -> routing fallback -> model-v1-quant)
- Sample failing prompt ids captured in bench/errors.log (bench/errors-2026-06-16.log)

Next steps for follow-up session (schedule)
- Re-run with client SDK change (Arjun) + KV residency probe (Chen) enabled. Focus: measure reduction in tail amplification. Tentative: 2026-06-23 afternoon window.
- Coordinate with Evals (quick 1-2 test prompts) before toggling fallback-wide.

Misc scratch TODOs (low priority)
- Add small synthetic test to perf lab that injects header auth delay at the network layer rather than shim to better emulate long-haul auth calls.
- Explore per-customer routing windowing to avoid global allocator backpressure during auth outages.

End of notes.

(rough, partially formatted. Will flesh out into a playbook section once follow-ups complete)
